newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India sells 50,000/t Oct naphtha, NWE minus $19/t.
newsitem.headline: India sells 50,000/t Oct naphtha, NWE minus $19/t.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has sold by tender 50,000 tonnes of naphtha to a Swiss trader at $19.00 per tonne below Northwest European (NWE) spot quotes on a free-on-board basis, traders said on Monday.

IOC sold the two 25,000-tonne cargoes lifting from east coast port of Madras, at the same price although one was for high aromatic naphtha lifting between October 3-5 and the other was low aromatic naphtha lifting October 7-9.
The tender closed on September 19 and was valid until September 20.
Traders said the cargoes were likely to head to the strong western markets in the U.S. and Europe.
In its last tender, IOC sold a high aromatic cargo at $25.84 below NWE quotes for a September 27-29 lifting from Bombay, on the west coast.
